inventory_disagreements.what: V17-E has 7 contests (Cooking, Building, Research / Invention, Sculpture, Story / Song, Farming, Children's Games; headings at L8384, 8403, 8412, 8422, 8432, 8444, 8452). Inventory part 3 counted 6, so V17 holds 34 contests, not 33, and the collection 177 events and add-ons, not 176.
The Wall starts at L4595 (its separator); L4594 is the blank line after the material banks. Inventory part 2 said 4594.
The game-exclusive events are grouped under per-game headings (VV2 - THE LOST CHILDREN, ...) that the inventory did not assign; each heading belongs to its group's first event here.
'END OF ...' lines the inventory did not assign: L8030 is its own notes row; L8900 belongs to the Isolan Decathlon, L9363 to the relic notes.

VIRTUAL VILLAGERS — ISOLA GRAND EVENT COLLECTION, V18
AUTHORSHIP, CONCEPT & REVISION CREDITS

Original user-author and creative director: Lorsieab2
Collaborating writer and expansion author: ChatGPT (OpenAI)

CREDIT POLICY
* "Original concept" identifies who first supplied the premise, mechanism,
  character direction, or material for an event; it does NOT necessarily
  mean that person drafted the prose.
* "Original event text" identifies who wrote the earliest event manuscript.
* "Additional writing" identifies new dialogue, branches, outcomes and
  event text written by the named contributor.
* "Substantial revision/expansion" identifies a major later rewrite or
  extension, without transferring ownership of the original work.
* "Creative direction" credits requested themes, constraints, and outcomes.
* Editorial formatting and small grammatical fixes do not count as
  original authorship or a substantial rewrite.
* Uncertain provenance is not silently attributed to either contributor.

USER-ORIGINATED EVENT TEXT — Lorsieab2
* The Cooking Contest (VV2): original premise, original event manuscript,
  randomized cook-off framework and extensive outcome banks by Lorsieab2.
  Later additional branches, repairs and expansion text: ChatGPT.
* The Child of Legend (VV1): original premise and original event manuscript
  by Lorsieab2. Later editing and/or expansion where present: ChatGPT.
* The Meaning of Faith (VV5): original premise and original event manuscript
  by Lorsieab2. Later editing and/or expansion where present: ChatGPT.
* The Aspiring Adventurer (VV1–VV5): original event and revised event text
  supplied by Lorsieab2; the separately supplied revised version is the
  source of record. Do not reassign its writing to ChatGPT.
* The Cave Explorers (VV1), The Climb (VV2), The Troubling Signs (VV3),
  Diving for Treasure (VV3), The Mysterious Mask (VV4), The Playful
  Dolphins (VV4), The Remembrance Ceremony (all five), and The Rumblings
  (all five): original event texts and mechanics supplied by Lorsieab2
  in the separate "More Island Events" manuscript. They are NOT
  automatically claimed as ChatGPT-authored just because referenced here.

CHATGPT-WRITTEN EVENTS — WITH LORSIEAB2 CREATIVE DIRECTION
* Universal events 1–5 (Grand Isolan Scholasticon; Great Beautification
  Project; Doctors' Dilemma; Everybody's a Winner?; Great Isolan
  Storytelling Contest): event prose and branching written by ChatGPT,
  developed in response to Lorsieab2's requested scope and themes.
* VV5 woodworking showcase, potluck dispute, laundry misunderstanding,
  neighborly games, keeper of little things and festival events:
  event prose/branches by ChatGPT; overarching VV5 two-community setup,
  Guardians of Harmony naming and gameplay constraints by Lorsieab2.
* V6–V8 additional VV1–VV5 event prose, variants and codas:
  ChatGPT, with Lorsieab2's canon guidance, character preferences,
  requests for emotional complexity and patcher constraints.
* V9 "Age of Terrible Ideas": event prose, material applications,
  trial and consequence branches by ChatGPT. Core requests for intense
  conflict, fights, false guilt, courts, imprisonment, reconciliation,
  and the sixteen specific bizarre materials by Lorsieab2.
* V10 reputation, appointment, school and rivalry events: event prose
  and detailed branching by ChatGPT. Requested social outcomes and
  leadership roles, including ostracism, laughingstock, village idiot,
  mad scientist, trusted advisor, teacher and heads of professions:
  Lorsieab2. VV3–VV5-only Magic/Nature faction rule: Lorsieab2.
* V11 The Secret of Life: central concept of a life-obsessed researcher
  resembling the classic overreaching creator archetype, without outside
  character references, by Lorsieab2. Full Isola-specific story text,
  branching and additional outcomes by ChatGPT.
* V11 The Council of Impossible Ideas and The Department of Terrible
  Ideas: central direction to write wildly implausible, seemingly
  useless, laughable and occasionally successful inventions by
  Lorsieab2. Specific new invention examples, dialogue, event prose,
  branches and outcomes developed by ChatGPT unless previously
  supplied by Lorsieab2 (including the snail-shell and other
  material prompts).

SIGNIFICANT COLLABORATIVE DEVELOPMENT
Lorsieab2 originated the ongoing collection's worldbuilding requirements,
selection of games, preferred emotional and comedic range, faction and
protected-character constraints, and numerous event premises and outcome
mechanics. ChatGPT significantly expanded the event collection through
new story prose, branches, randomized dialogue, reputation systems,
continuity notes and integration guidance. These are distinct credits:
"Concept / creative direction: Lorsieab2" and "Event writing and
substantial expansion: ChatGPT" are both appropriate for many events.

ATTRIBUTION LIMITS
This credit ledger describes contributions identifiable from the user-
supplied event manuscripts and the cumulative v11 collection. It does
not claim that every paragraph has been compared against every historical
revision. Where a specific sentence's provenance is uncertain, the
original manuscript author retains the original-text credit, and
ChatGPT receives credit only for identifiable additions or substantial
expansions. The separately uploaded "More Island Events" manuscript
and "Aspiring Adventurer" manuscript remain Lorsieab2-authored source
materials; they are not silently incorporated as ChatGPT writing.

source_check.heading: L5: EVENT RM-01  -  THE FAIR SHARE SETUP: After a difficult harvest, a farmer notices that the food portions are uneven, and several families are still waiting. A. Divide the remaining food into equal portions. A1. Every waiting family receives something, though the portions are smaller than hoped. A2. The farmer discovers that equal portions leave a larger household struggling and reconsiders the distribution. B. Ask each household what it needs. B1. The families agree on portions that account for their different circumstances. B2. The discussion takes longer than expected, but nobody is overlooked. C. Give the largest portion to the household that worked hardest. C1. The workers appreciate the recognition but ask that the youngest children be fed first. C2. An elder points out that some villagers contributed in ways the farmer did not see. D. Invite another farmer to check the distribution. D1. The second farmer notices a counting mistake, and the portions are corrected. D2. The two disagree over what is fairest and agree to consult the waiting families.

source_check.heading: L39: EVENT RM-18  -  THE TREE WITH FRUIT SETUP: A family finds a tree heavy with ripe fruit, while several branches also shelter feeding birds. A. Gather only the fruit within easy reach. A1. The family collects enough for supper without disturbing the birds. A2. Much of the fruit remains high above them, and they decide to return another day. B. Collect fallen fruit that is still sound. B1. The family fills a small basket and leaves the branches untouched. B2. Most fallen fruit is spoiled, so they seek food elsewhere. C. Ask an experienced gatherer how much to take. C1. The gatherer explains how to harvest without damaging the tree. C2. The gatherer recommends waiting until more fruit ripens. D. Share the harvest with neighboring households. D1. Several families enjoy a small portion of fresh fruit. D2. The fruit is insufficient for everyone, and the family agrees to gather more when available.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L9: 01. The First Armorer  -  An artisan experiments with layered bark, woven fibers, and leather to create protective clothing. Villagers debate whether to keep it ready for emergencies or display it as a symbol of preparedness.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L10: 02. The Wooden Breastplate  -  A craftsperson finishes a carved breastplate. Its beautiful designs attract admiration, but an elder wonders whether decoration has compromised its usefulness.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L11: 03. The Woven Armor  -  Tightly woven fibers make a surprisingly sturdy protective garment. Several villagers volunteer to learn the technique.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L12: 04. The Ceremonial Helmet  -  A helmet decorated with feathers, shells, and carved symbols is unveiled for a festival. Nobody agrees who should wear it.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L13: 05. The Armorer's Mistake  -  A new piece of protective gear restricts its wearer's movement. The armorer must reconsider the design.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L14: 06. The Old Suit of Armor  -  Weathered protective equipment is found in an abandoned shelter. Its origins and former owner remain unknown.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L15: 07. The Shieldmaker's Apprentice  -  An apprentice struggles to balance a wooden shield. Their mentor explains that good craft requires patience as well as strength.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L16: 08. The Armor of Remembrance  -  A family preserves a ceremonial breastplate worn by an ancestor during a troubled era. They disagree about whether it belongs at home or in a communal memorial.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L17: 09. The Spearmaker's Craft  -  An artisan makes spears for hunting, ceremony, and village defense. An apprentice notices that each carries a different meaning.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L18: 10. The Bowyer's Workshop  -  A bowmaker experiments with different woods and fibers, drawing curious villagers to the workshop.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L19: 11. The Arrowmaker's Dilemma  -  An artisan must divide limited feathers and wood between a ceremonial collection and replacing worn hunting arrows.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L20: 12. The Ceremonial Spear  -  A carved spear is presented to an elder, who reminds the village that the symbol represents responsibility, not superiority.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L21: 13. The Broken Bow  -  A hunter discovers a crack in a treasured inherited bow. Repairing it might preserve its usefulness; retiring it might better protect its history.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L22: 14. The Practice Targets  -  Villagers establish an archery practice area away from homes. Their friendly competition becomes popular.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L23: 15. The Spear Dance  -  Performers rehearse a dance using decorated, blunted spears. They debate how much the movements should change over time.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L24: 16. The Ancient Arrowheads  -  Weathered arrowheads are uncovered. Scholars disagree about whether they were used for hunting, defense, or ceremony.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L25: 17. The Hunter's Walking Stick  -  A hunter carries a staff useful for walking, navigating difficult terrain, and protection against dangerous wildlife.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L26: 18. The Keeper of the Implements  -  An elder maintains bows, spears, shields, and traditional tools. Some see equipment; others see an archive of ingenuity.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L27: 19. The Farmer's Implements  -  Farmers note that hoes, digging sticks, and other everyday tools could also protect people during an emergency.

credit.text:
ISOLA — ARMOR, WEAPONS, AND INHERITED TRADITIONS
Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L28: 20. The Sturdy Staff  -  A carpenter makes wooden staffs used for walking, carrying supplies, performances, and defensive practice.

credit.text:

Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L29: 21. The Harvesting Blade  -  An artisan repairs a harvesting tool. Its owner reflects on how an implement intended to sustain life might also be needed for protection.

credit.text:

source_check.heading: L30: 22. The Fisherman's Spear  -  A fisher demonstrates a traditional fishing spear and discusses the different roles similar implements have held in Isola's history.

Standalone event and flavor-text expansion

source_check.heading: L31: 23. The Village Storehouse  -  Villagers reorganize farming tools, hunting gear, protective equipment, and ceremonial objects so each is accessible and cared for.
